maya: FYI I'm planning to enable the route-level flag `seg-fallback` for the /search route tomorrow morning for the canary audience. Quick question about inheritance semantics — want to make sure we don't accidentally expose model variants.

maya: Concrete: we have org -> project -> route -> model scopes. If a route defines audiences A,B and a project defines audiences A,B,C, does enabling at route replace the project list or merge with it? Also what happens if model toggles conflict (eg modelX disabled at model scope but enabled at route scope)? Example config below: 

maya: ```
org: { flags: { new_rerank: on } }
project: { flags: { new_rerank: on, segmentation: [A,B,C] } }
route(/search): { flags: { segmentation: [A,B], seg-fallback: project } }
model(modelX): { flags: { new_rerank: off } }
```

sam: Short answer: more specific scope wins. model > route > project > org. If the route sets `segmentation` explicitly it replaces the project list unless the flag supports an explicit merge option. We have a `merge_audiences: true` opt-in for some flags, but it defaults to replace.

sam: For your `seg-fallback` idea: when route has `seg-fallback: project` we evaluate audiences on route first; if no match, we check project audiences. Fallbacks are evaluated in order you list them.

sam: Model-level toggles are highest precedence for that model instance. So modelX disabled at model scope will stay disabled even if route enables it — that's by design so teams can quickly kill a misbehaving model without touching route config.

kai: +1 to model being able to kill. One nuance: if route-level rollout is a traffic-split that sends 20% to modelX and modelX is disabled at model scope, runtime will divert that 20% to the fallback variant (route's fallback_model) — make sure you have fallback configured.

olivia: A couple of guardrails to keep in mind:
- Always set a safety threshold `auto-disable-on-error: 0.05` at route or project level for canaries.
- For production rollouts, use `default-off` when enabling new behavior that touches user-visible UX.
- Add a telemetry hook for model-level errors, we currently support `on_error_disable: true` that can flip model flags automatically.

maya: Good notes. Do we have a standard for canary audience sizes? I was thinking 2% first, then 10%, 50%.

sam: We usually recommend: 1) smoke/internal 0.1% (dev), 2) canary 2-5%, 3) ramp 25%, 4) full. Depends on traffic volume. Always have rollback thresholds.

kai: Also watch cache warming: when you change segmentation lists the KV cache may drop for some prefixes and spike latency. Consider pre-warming or a staged TTL change.

olivia: For observability, ensure you add these metrics in the rollout config: `flag_eval_success`, `flag_eval_errors`, `model_inference_errors`, `latency_p50/p95`. We have dashboard templates under Redwood Console -> Rollouts.

maya: Thanks — I'll set route segmentation to [A,B] only and set `seg-fallback: project` and `merge_audiences: false` (explicit replace). I'll also enable `auto-disable-on-error: 0.03` and hook the rollout dashboard.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled by @maya for route /search at 2025-03-19T09:00Z :rocket: (canary 2%, fallback -> project audiences)

sam: If anything looks off after the deploy ping here and I'll help flip model-level toggles. :eyes:
